text: The modern periodic table is based on the:
explanation: Moseley's Modern Periodic Law states that properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic numbers.

text: Elements in the same group of the periodic table have the same:
explanation: Elements in the same group have the same number of valence electrons, giving similar chemical properties.

text: Atomic radius increases as you go:
options: Across a period left to right
explanation: Atomic radius increases down a group as new electron shells are added. It decreases across a period due to increasing nuclear charge.

text: Which of the following has the highest electronegativity?
explanation: Fluorine (F) has the highest electronegativity (3.98 on Pauling scale) of all elements.

text: An element has electron configuration 2,8,7. It belongs to:
explanation: 3 shells → Period 3. 7 valence electrons → Group 17 (halogen). Element is Chlorine.

text: Ionization energy generally increases:
options: From metals to noble gases is wrong
explanation: Ionization energy increases across a period as nuclear charge increases and atomic radius decreases, making it harder to remove electrons.

text: An ionic bond is formed by:
options: Transfer of electrons from metal to non-metal
explanation: Ionic bonds form when electrons transfer from a metal (low IE) to a non-metal (high EA), creating oppositely charged ions.

text: A covalent bond is formed by:
options: Sharing of electrons between non-metal atoms
explanation: Covalent bonds form when non-metal atoms share electron pairs to achieve stable configurations.

text: Which of the following is an ionic compound?
explanation: NaCl (sodium chloride) is ionic — Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions held by electrostatic attraction. HCl, CO₂, NH₃ are covalent.

text: The type of bond present in N₂ molecule is:
explanation: N₂ has a triple bond (N≡N) — nitrogen shares 3 pairs of electrons to achieve octet.

text: Coordinate (dative) bond is formed when:
options: Both electrons in the shared pair come from one atom
explanation: A coordinate bond (or dative covalent bond) is formed when one atom donates both electrons of the shared pair to another atom.

text: An acid is a substance that:
explanation: Arrhenius defined an acid as a substance that donates H⁺ (proton) ions when dissolved in water.

text: The pH of a neutral solution at 25°C is:
explanation: A neutral solution has equal H⁺ and OH⁻ concentrations → pH = 7 at 25°C.

text: Which of the following turns litmus red?
explanation: Acids turn blue litmus red. HCl is an acid. NaOH is a base (turns red litmus blue). NaCl and Na₂CO₃ are basic/neutral salts.

text: Salt formed by a strong acid and weak base will have pH:
explanation: Salt of strong acid + weak base (e.g., NH₄Cl) hydrolyses to give an acidic solution (pH < 7).

text: When dilute HCl reacts with Na₂CO₃, the gas evolved is:
explanation: Na₂CO₃ + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H₂O + CO₂↑. Carbon dioxide is evolved, turning limewater milky.

text: The flame test for sodium gives:
explanation: Sodium gives a characteristic golden yellow (intense) flame in the flame test.

text: Which reagent is used to test for chloride ions?
explanation: Chloride ions are detected with acidified silver nitrate (AgNO₃) solution — a white precipitate of AgCl forms, insoluble in dilute HNO₃.

text: Nessler's reagent is used to test for:
explanation: Nessler's reagent (K₂[HgI₄] in NaOH) turns brown/orange-brown in the presence of ammonia.

text: A white precipitate soluble in excess NaOH indicates the presence of:
explanation: Al(OH)₃ is amphoteric — it dissolves in excess NaOH to form aluminate [Al(OH)₄]⁻. White, then soluble = Al³⁺.

text: Iron(III) ions give which colour with NaOH solution?
explanation: Fe³⁺ + 3OH⁻ → Fe(OH)₃ ↓ (reddish-brown/rust-coloured precipitate insoluble in excess NaOH).

text: Ammonia is manufactured by the:
explanation: Ammonia (NH₃) is manufactured industrially by the Haber process: N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ (450°C, 200 atm, iron catalyst).

text: Ammonia turns moist red litmus:
explanation: Ammonia is alkaline and turns moist red litmus paper blue.

text: The catalyst used in the Haber process is:
explanation: The Haber process uses iron as catalyst with molybdenum (or K₂O, Al₂O₃) as promoters.

text: When ammonia gas is passed over heated copper oxide, the products are:
explanation: 4NH₃ + 3CuO → 3Cu + 3H₂O + N₂. Ammonia reduces CuO (black) to Cu (pink/red), itself oxidised to N₂.

text: The industrial oxidation of ammonia (Ostwald process) produces:
explanation: Ostwald process: 4NH₃ + 5O₂ → 4NO + 6H₂O (with Pt catalyst at 850°C). NO is then oxidised to NO₂, dissolved in water to give HNO₃.

text: Sulphuric acid is manufactured by:
explanation: H₂SO₄ is manufactured by the Contact process: SO₂ → SO₃ (with V₂O₅ catalyst) → H₂SO₄.

text: The catalyst used in the Contact process is:
explanation: The Contact process uses vanadium pentoxide (V₂O₅) as catalyst at 450°C to oxidise SO₂ to SO₃.

text: Dilute sulphuric acid reacts with zinc to produce:
explanation: Zn + H₂SO₄ (dilute) → ZnSO₄ + H₂↑. Hydrogen gas is evolved.

text: Concentrated H₂SO₄ acts as a dehydrating agent when it converts sugar (C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁) to:
explanation: Conc. H₂SO₄ removes H and O as water from sugar, leaving behind black spongy carbon: C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁ → 12C + 11H₂O.

text: Nitric acid is manufactured by the:
explanation: HNO₃ is manufactured industrially by the Ostwald process (catalytic oxidation of ammonia).

text: When conc. HNO₃ reacts with copper, the gas evolved is:
explanation: Cu + 4HNO₃(conc.) → Cu(NO₃)₂ + 2H₂O + 2NO₂↑. Brown fumes of nitrogen dioxide are evolved.

text: Dilute HNO₃ reacts with copper to give:
explanation: 3Cu + 8HNO₃(dilute) → 3Cu(NO₃)₂ + 4H₂O + 2NO↑. Colourless NO is evolved (turns brown in air as it oxidises to NO₂).

text: The general formula of alkanes is:
explanation: Alkanes (saturated hydrocarbons) have the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ (e.g., methane CH₄, ethane C₂H₆).

text: Alkenes contain:
explanation: Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons with at least one C=C double bond (e.g., ethene C₂H₄).

text: The reaction of ethene with HBr is an example of:
explanation: Alkenes undergo addition reactions where atoms add across the C=C double bond: CH₂=CH₂ + HBr → CH₃CH₂Br.

text: Fermentation of glucose produces:
explanation: C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂ (yeast/zymase catalysed at ~35°C).

text: The IUPAC name of CH₃—CH(OH)—CH₃ is:
explanation: The OH group is on the second carbon of a 3-carbon chain → propan-2-ol (isopropanol).

text: Electrolysis is the:
options: Decomposition of electrolyte by passing electric current
Production of electricity from chemical reactions
explanation: Electrolysis is the decomposition of an electrolyte (ionic compound in solution or melt) by passing direct electric current through it.

text: During electrolysis, reduction occurs at the:
explanation: At the cathode (negative electrode): cations gain electrons (reduction). At anode: anions lose electrons (oxidation).

text: During electrolysis of dilute sulphuric acid, oxygen is evolved at the:
explanation: At anode (+): 4OH⁻ → 2H₂O + O₂ + 4e⁻. Oxygen is liberated. At cathode: H⁺ + e⁻ → H₂.

text: Copper plating of an object uses:
options: Copper sulphate solution with copper anode
explanation: Electroplating with copper uses CuSO₄ solution, copper anode (which dissolves), and the object as cathode.

text: According to Faraday's first law of electrolysis, the mass of substance deposited is:
options: Proportional to quantity of charge passed
explanation: Faraday's first law: m ∝ Q (charge = current × time). Greater charge → more substance deposited.

text: One mole of any substance contains:
explanation: One mole of any substance contains Avogadro's number of particles: 6.022 × 10²³ (atoms, molecules, ions, etc.).

text: The molar mass of H₂O is:
The number of moles in 44 g of CO₂ is:
explanation: M(CO₂) = 12 + 32 = 44 g/mol. Moles = 44/44 = 1 mol.

text: The volume of 1 mole of any gas at STP (Standard Temperature and Pressure) is:
explanation: At STP (0°C, 1 atm), 1 mole of any ideal gas occupies 22.4 litres (the molar volume).

text: How many molecules are present in 0.25 mol of water?
The element with atomic number 19 belongs to:
explanation: Z=19 is Potassium (K). Configuration: 2,8,8,1. One valence electron → Group 1. Four shells → Period 4.

text: The type of reaction: HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O is called:
explanation: Acid + Base → Salt + Water is a neutralisation reaction.

text: Which of the following is an alkyne?
explanation: C₂H₂ (acetylene/ethyne) is an alkyne with a C≡C triple bond. Alkynes have formula CₙH₂ₙ₋₂.

text: In electrolysis of brine (NaCl solution), chlorine is evolved at the:
explanation: 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻ occurs at anode. Products: Cl₂ at anode, H₂ at cathode, NaOH in solution.

text: Concentrated H₂SO₄ is stored in:
explanation: Conc. H₂SO₄ is stored in glass or iron vessels — it passivates (forms protective oxide layer on) iron and doesn't react with glass.

text: In the Haber process, an increase in pressure:
options: Increases yield of NH₃ (Le Chatelier's principle)
explanation: N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ involves 4 moles of reactants → 2 moles of product. Increased pressure favours the side with fewer gas moles (products) → more NH₃.

text: The test for CO₂ gas is:
explanation: CO₂ turns clear limewater milky (Ca(OH)₂ + CO₂ → CaCO₃↓ + H₂O). CaCO₃ is the white precipitate.

text: Which of the following has a giant covalent structure?
explanation: Diamond has a giant covalent (macromolecular) structure where each carbon is bonded to 4 others in a tetrahedral lattice — making it very hard and with a very high melting point.

text: Which property decreases across a period from left to right?
explanation: Atomic radius decreases across a period as nuclear charge increases with same number of shells, pulling electrons closer.

text: Aqua regia is a mixture of:
options: Conc. HNO₃ and Conc. HCl in 1:3 ratio
explanation: Aqua regia (royal water) = 1 part conc. HNO₃ + 3 parts conc. HCl. It dissolves gold and platinum by forming soluble chloro-complexes.

text: The substitution reaction of methane with Cl₂ in sunlight produces:
explanation: Free radical substitution of CH₄ with Cl₂ in UV light can progressively replace H atoms: CH₃Cl → CH₂Cl₂ → CHCl₃ → CCl₄.

text: Empirical formula of a compound with 40% C, 6.67% H and 53.33% O is:
explanation: Mole ratio: C: 40/12=3.33, H: 6.67/1=6.67, O: 53.33/16=3.33. Ratio = 1:2:1. Empirical formula = CH₂O.

text: When excess CO₂ is passed through limewater, the turbidity:
explanation: CaCO₃ + CO₂ + H₂O → Ca(HCO₃)₂ (soluble). Excess CO₂ converts the insoluble carbonate to soluble bicarbonate, clearing the turbidity.

text: During purification of copper by electrolysis:
options: Impure copper is anode, pure copper is cathode
Pure copper is anode, impure is cathode
explanation: In electrolytic refining of copper, impure copper is anode (dissolves), Cu²⁺ ions migrate to cathode (pure copper), which grows. Impurities fall as anode mud.

text: The bond angle in H₂O is approximately:
explanation: H₂O has a bent/angular structure with bond angle ≈ 104.5° due to 2 lone pairs on oxygen repelling the bonding pairs.

text: A gas that turns moist lead acetate paper black is:
explanation: H₂S turns moist lead acetate paper black: H₂S + Pb(CH₃COO)₂ → PbS (black) + 2CH₃COOH.

text: Nitric acid does NOT react with:
explanation: Gold (and platinum) are noble metals that do not react with nitric acid alone. They dissolve only in aqua regia.

text: The industrial process for producing H₂SO₄ uses which intermediate?
explanation: SO₃ is not dissolved in water directly (forms acid mist). Instead, SO₃ is absorbed in 98% H₂SO₄ to form oleum (H₂SO₄·SO₃), then diluted.

text: The number of atoms in 12 g of carbon is:
explanation: 12 g of C = 1 mole of C = 6.022 × 10²³ atoms (by definition of the mole, based on ¹²C).

text: Petroleum is a mixture of:
explanation: Petroleum (crude oil) is a complex mixture of mainly hydrocarbons (alkanes, cycloalkanes) with small amounts of other compounds.

text: Noble gases have:
explanation: Noble gases (Group 18) have completely filled outer electron shells (2 for He, 8 for others), making them highly stable and unreactive.

text: Universal indicator shows which colour for neutral solution?
explanation: Universal indicator shows green colour for neutral solutions (pH 7), red/orange for acids, blue/violet for bases.

text: Electroplating is used to:
options: Coat a metal with a thin layer of another metal
explanation: Electroplating deposits a thin layer of one metal onto another using electrolysis, often for protection or decoration.

text: Which of the following is a non-polar covalent compound?
explanation: H₂ is non-polar covalent — identical atoms share electrons equally. HCl, NH₃, H₂O have polar bonds due to electronegativity differences.

text: Ammonia is collected by:
explanation: Ammonia is less dense than air and highly soluble in water. It is collected by downward displacement of air (upward displacement inverted over air). Correct: ammonia is collected by downward displacement of air.

text: The colour of NO₂ gas is:
explanation: Nitrogen dioxide (NO₂) is a reddish-brown (or dark brown) pungent gas.

text: When dilute H₂SO₄ is added to BaCl₂ solution, a white precipitate of _____ forms.
explanation: Ba²⁺ + SO₄²⁻ → BaSO₄↓ (white). Barium sulphate is insoluble in dilute acids — used to confirm sulphate ions.

text: What volume does 4 g of oxygen gas occupy at STP?
Ethanol burns in oxygen to form:
explanation: C₂H₅OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O. Complete combustion of ethanol gives carbon dioxide and water.

text: Which test identifies the presence of starch?
explanation: Iodine solution (iodine in KI) turns blue-black in the presence of starch — a standard test for starch.

text: Metallic bonding is best described as:
options: Lattice of positive ions in a sea of delocalised electrons
Sharing of electrons between two atoms
explanation: In a metallic bond, metal atoms lose valence electrons to form positive ions embedded in a 'sea' of freely moving (delocalised) electrons.

text: Which of the following shows the strongest metallic character?
explanation: Metallic character increases down a group. Caesium (Period 6, Group 1) has the lowest ionization energy among common elements, making it the most metallic.

text: An acid with pH = 2 is how many times more acidic than one with pH = 4?
explanation: pH 2 has H⁺ concentration = 10⁻² M; pH 4 has 10⁻⁴ M. Ratio = 10⁻²/10⁻⁴ = 100 times.

text: During electrolysis of molten NaCl, sodium is deposited at the:
explanation: Na⁺ + e⁻ → Na at cathode (reduction). Cl⁻ → ½Cl₂ + e⁻ at anode (oxidation).

text: Which reaction is used to distinguish between an alkane and an alkene?
options: Bromine water test — alkene decolourises it
explanation: Alkenes decolourise bromine water (orange/brown → colourless) due to addition of Br₂ across C=C. Alkanes do not react with Br₂(aq).

text: Ammonia is a:
options: Covalent compound with lone pair on nitrogen
explanation: NH₃ is a covalent molecule. Nitrogen has one lone pair, making NH₃ a Lewis base and responsible for its basic properties.

text: Iron does not react with concentrated HNO₃ because:
options: It forms a passive protective oxide layer
explanation: Iron (and also aluminium) becomes passive in conc. HNO₃ — a thin oxide film forms on the surface, preventing further reaction.

text: The percentage of nitrogen by mass in NH₃ is:
The shape of BF₃ molecule is:
explanation: BF₃ has 3 bonding pairs around boron (no lone pairs) → trigonal planar shape with bond angle 120°.

text: H₂SO₄ is called:
explanation: Concentrated sulphuric acid is historically called 'oil of vitriol'. HCl is spirit of salt; HNO₃ is aqua fortis; aqua regia is HNO₃+HCl mixture.

text: The functional group present in alcohols is:
explanation: Alcohols contain the hydroxyl (–OH) functional group. –COOH = carboxyl (acids), –CHO = aldehyde, –CO– = ketone.

text: The flame test for potassium gives:
explanation: Potassium (K) gives a characteristic lilac (pale purple/violet) flame in the flame test.

text: Sodium carbonate (washing soda) solution is:
explanation: Na₂CO₃ is a salt of strong base (NaOH) and weak acid (H₂CO₃). It hydrolyses to give an alkaline (basic) solution.

text: Metalloids (semimetals) are located:
options: Along the staircase between metals and non-metals
explanation: Metalloids (Si, Ge, As, Sb, Te, B, etc.) are located along the dividing line (staircase) between metals and non-metals in the periodic table.

text: The electrolyte used in electroplating with silver is:
explanation: Silver plating uses potassium argentocyanide K[Ag(CN)₂] or silver nitrate solution as electrolyte, with a silver anode.

text: The simplest alkane is:
explanation: Methane (CH₄) is the simplest alkane (n=1 in CₙH₂ₙ₊₂).

text: The compound with the highest melting point is:
explanation: NaCl has a giant ionic lattice structure with strong electrostatic forces → very high melting point (801°C). CO₂, H₂O, CH₄ are covalent molecular with lower melting points.

text: Ammonia is dried by passing through:
explanation: Ammonia is an alkaline gas. Acidic drying agents (H₂SO₄, P₂O₅) would react with it. Neutral CaCl₂ forms a complex with NH₃. Quicklime (CaO) is used to dry ammonia.

text: Which has more atoms: 18 g H₂O or 44 g CO₂?
options: 44 g CO₂ (3 moles of atoms — equal)
explanation: 18 g H₂O = 1 mol → 3 moles of atoms (2H+1O). 44 g CO₂ = 1 mol → 3 moles of atoms (1C+2O). Both have the same number of atoms.

text: The brown ring test is used to detect:
explanation: The brown ring test: Fe²⁺ + NO → Fe(NO)²⁺ (brown ring at junction of H₂SO₄ and FeSO₄ layers). Tests for NO₃⁻ ions.

text: H₂SO₄ reacts with copper on heating to produce:
explanation: Cu + 2H₂SO₄(hot conc.) → CuSO₄ + SO₂↑ + 2H₂O. Hot conc. H₂SO₄ is an oxidising acid, oxidising Cu to Cu²⁺.

text: Which gas is produced when an ammonium salt is heated with alkali?
explanation: NH₄Cl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O + NH₃↑. Ammonia is released — turns moist red litmus blue, gives white fumes with HCl.

text: Denatured alcohol is ethanol mixed with:
options: Methanol (to make it unfit for drinking)
explanation: Denatured alcohol has methanol (and other additives like pyridine) added to make it toxic for consumption, used as industrial solvent.

text: The element silicon is classified as:
explanation: Silicon (Si) is a metalloid — it has properties intermediate between metals and non-metals. It is a semiconductor.

text: NaCl dissolves in water because:
options: Water molecules solvate the ions (ionic-dipole forces)
explanation: Polar water molecules surround and solvate Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions, overcoming the lattice energy and dissolving the crystal.

text: The temperature used in the Haber process is approximately:
explanation: Haber process uses 400–500°C (optimum ≈ 450°C) — a compromise between rate and equilibrium yield (higher T = more rate but less yield).

text: A compound contains only C and H. It has 80% C by mass. The empirical formula is:
explanation: C: 80/12=6.67 mol; H: 20/1=20 mol. Ratio = 6.67:20 = 1:3. Empirical formula = CH₃.

text: Vinegar contains:
explanation: Vinegar is a dilute solution of ethanoic (acetic) acid, CH₃COOH, typically 4–8%.

text: Electrolytes are substances that:
options: Conduct electricity in solution or when molten
explanation: Electrolytes (acids, bases, salts) ionise in water or when molten, allowing electrical conduction.

text: The reaction of ethanol with sodium produces:
explanation: 2C₂H₅OH + 2Na → 2C₂H₅ONa + H₂↑. Sodium replaces the acidic H of the OH group to give sodium ethoxide and hydrogen gas.

text: Which of the following has the weakest intermolecular forces?
explanation: CH₄ has only weak London dispersion forces (non-polar). H₂O, NH₃, and HF have stronger hydrogen bonding.

text: To confirm the presence of sulphate ions, we add:
explanation: SO₄²⁻ + Ba²⁺ → BaSO₄↓ (white, insoluble in HCl). Acidifying with HCl first rules out other white precipitates (BaCO₃, BaSO₃ — these dissolve in HCl).

text: An amphiprotic substance can:
options: Act as both acid and donor of protons, and as base accepting protons
explanation: Amphiprotic substances (like H₂O, HCO₃⁻, HSO₄⁻, NH₃) can act as both Bronsted-Lowry acids (proton donors) and bases (proton acceptors).

text: When NaHCO₃ is added to H₂SO₄, which gas is produced?
explanation: NaHCO₃ + H₂SO₄ → Na₂SO₄ + H₂O + CO₂↑. Carbon dioxide is evolved.

text: The most electronegative element in the periodic table is:
explanation: Fluorine (F) has the highest electronegativity value (3.98 Pauling scale) — it is the most electronegative element.

text: How many grams of CO₂ contain 1.505 × 10²³ molecules?
Carbohydrates are made up of:
options: C, H, O in specific ratios
explanation: Carbohydrates have empirical formula (CH₂O)ₙ — they contain carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen.

text: An element X has atomic number 19 (Period 4, Group 1). It forms an oxide with formula:
explanation: Group 1 elements have valency 1. Oxide formula = X₂O (like K₂O). [Board 2017] XO: Group 2 valency; X₂O₃: Group 13; XO₂: Group 14 or dioxide-forming metals.

text: The type of bond present in NH₃ molecule is:
explanation: NH₃ has 3 N-H covalent bonds formed by sharing of electrons. [Board 2017] It also has one lone pair (base of co-ordinate bond with H⁺), but primary bond type is covalent. Ionic requires metal-nonmetal; metallic is in metals.

text: Dilute HNO₃ reacts with copper to produce:
explanation: Dilute HNO₃ + Cu → Cu(NO₃)₂ + NO↑ + H₂O. Copper doesn't displace H₂ from acids; CuSO₄ involves H₂SO₄; CuO is with O₂. [Board 2017] 3Cu + 8HNO₃(dilute) → 3Cu(NO₃)₂ + 2NO + 4H₂O.

text: Mass of 3.011 × 10²³ molecules of CO₂ (M=44) is:
explanation: 3.011×10²³ = Avogadro's number/2 = 0.5 mol. Mass = 0.5×44 = 22 g. [Board 2017] 44 g = 1 mol; 11 g = 0.25 mol; 88 g = 2 mol.

text: Which of these metals can be extracted by electrolysis of its molten chloride?
explanation: Sodium (highly reactive) is extracted by electrolysis of molten NaCl (Down's process). Less reactive metals like Fe, Cu, Zn are extracted by reduction or electrolysis of aqueous solutions. [Board 2017]

text: The IUPAC name of CH₃−CH₂−OH is:
explanation: CH₃CH₂OH = 2 carbon chain with OH group = Ethanol. [Board 2017] Methanol = CH₃OH (1 carbon); Propanol = 3 carbons; Ethanoic acid = CH₃COOH.

text: When chlorine reacts with hot concentrated NaOH, the products are:
explanation: Cl₂ + 6NaOH(hot conc.) → 5NaCl + NaClO₃ + 3H₂O (disproportionation). [Board 2017] Cold dilute NaOH gives NaCl+NaOCl; NaClO₄ is not standard product; second option is cold NaOH product.

text: A gas that turns moist lead acetate paper black is:
explanation: H₂S turns lead acetate paper black due to PbS (black) formation. [Board 2017] SO₂ turns acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ green; CO₂ turns lime water milky; HCl turns moist blue litmus red.

text: During electrolysis of dilute H₂SO₄, the gas discharged at cathode is:
explanation: At cathode: 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂↑. Oxygen is liberated at anode. [Board 2017] SO₂ is not produced in dilute H₂SO₄ electrolysis; water vapour is not a direct electrolytic product.

text: The salt formed by neutralisation of Ca(OH)₂ with HCl is:
explanation: Ca(OH)₂ + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + 2H₂O. CaO is the oxide; Ca(HCO₃)₂ forms with CO₂; CaSO₄ forms with H₂SO₄. [Board 2017]

text: Volume of 0.1 mol of O₂ at STP (molar volume = 22.4 L):
The structure of water molecule is:
explanation: Water has 2 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs on oxygen. VSEPR theory predicts bent/V-shaped geometry (bond angle ≈104.5°). [Board 2018] Linear: CO₂; trigonal: BF₃; tetrahedral: CH₄.

text: Aluminium is refined by electrolytic refining. During this process, pure aluminium deposits at:
explanation: In electrolytic refining, impure metal is anode, pure metal deposits at cathode. [Board 2018] Anode dissolves; deposition at both is wrong; metal stays in solid/electrode form.

text: Which acid is used in the manufacture of fertilisers and explosives?
explanation: Nitric acid is used to make ammonium nitrate (fertiliser) and TNT (explosive). [Board 2018] HCl is used in cleaning/metal work; H₂SO₄ is used in batteries/industry; acetic acid is used in food/plastics.

text: Ethene (C₂H₄) undergoes addition reaction with bromine water. The product is:
explanation: CH₂=CH₂ + Br₂ → CH₂Br−CH₂Br (1,2-dibromoethane). Bromine water decolourises. [Board 2018] Bromoethane (C₂H₅Br) is from substitution; ethyl bromide is same as bromoethane; ethanol forms with H₂O.

text: Ammonia reacts with oxygen in the presence of platinum catalyst to form:
explanation: 4NH₃ + 5O₂ → 4NO + 6H₂O (Ostwald process, first step). NO is then oxidised to NO₂. [Board 2018] N₂ forms without catalyst; NO₂ is second step product; N₂O (nitrous oxide) is from NH₄NO₃ decomposition.

text: Noble gases are placed in Group 18. They are chemically inert because:
options: Their outermost shell is completely filled
They have high ionisation energy only
Their atomic radius is very small
explanation: Noble gases have completely filled valence shells (8 electrons, or 2 for He), making them chemically stable. [Board 2018] High IE is a consequence, not the primary cause; small radius is for H,He but not Xe; high electronegativity is for halogens.

text: In the electrolysis of brine (NaCl solution), what is discharged at the anode?
explanation: At anode: 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻. Chlorine ions are preferentially discharged over OH⁻. [Board 2018] H₂ is discharged at cathode; Na is not discharged from aqueous solution; O₂ would appear in dilute NaCl.

text: The method of extraction of zinc from zinc blende (ZnS) involves:
explanation: ZnS is roasted to ZnO, then reduced with coke: ZnO + C → Zn + CO. [Board 2018] Direct reduction of ZnS doesn't work efficiently; electrolysis is for Al; CO reduction is for iron not zinc.

text: White precipitate soluble in excess NaOH is given by the cation:
explanation: Al(OH)₃ is amphoteric — dissolves in excess NaOH to form [Al(OH)₄]⁻. [Board 2018] Ca(OH)₂ is slightly soluble, not amphoteric; Fe(OH)₃ is brown, insoluble in NaOH; Cu(OH)₂ is blue.

text: Concentrated H₂SO₄ acts as a dehydrating agent. This means it:
explanation: Conc. H₂SO₄ removes elements of water (H and OH) from compounds, e.g., dehydration of sugar (sucrose → carbon + water). [Board 2019] Reducing agent means electron donation; OH⁻ comes from bases; dilution is physical.

text: What mass of CaCO₃ must be heated to produce 11.2 L of CO₂ at STP?
explanation: 11.2 L = 0.5 mol CO₂. CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂. 0.5 mol CaCO₃ needed. Mass = 0.5 × 100 = 50 g. [Board 2019] 100 g = 1 mol (22.4 L); 25 g = 0.25 mol; 44 g = molar mass of CO₂.

text: The reaction of ethanol with sodium gives:
explanation: 2C₂H₅OH + 2Na → 2C₂H₅ONa + H₂↑. [Board 2019] Sodium + water is reaction of Na with H₂O; ethylene forms on dehydration with H₂SO₄; ether forms between two alcohols.

text: The bond in HCl is:
explanation: HCl has a covalent bond with unequal sharing (Cl is more electronegative), making it polar covalent (H⁺ᵟ−Clᵟ⁻). [Board 2019] Pure covalent = H₂, Cl₂; Ionic = NaCl; Metallic = Fe.

text: Sulphur dioxide is used as a bleaching agent. It bleaches by:
explanation: SO₂ bleaches by reduction (removes oxygen from coloured compounds). The bleaching is temporary as colour returns on oxidation by air. [Board 2019] Cl₂ bleaches by oxidation; chlorination adds Cl₂; dehydration is H₂SO₄ action.

text: Moving left to right across Period 3, the metallic character:
explanation: Metallic character decreases left to right in a period as ionisation energy increases (atoms hold onto electrons more tightly). Na > Mg > Al > Si > P > S > Cl. [Board 2019]

text: The ore of iron used in a blast furnace is:
explanation: Haematite (Fe₂O₃) is the principal ore of iron. [Board 2019] Galena is lead ore; Bauxite is aluminium ore; Malachite is copper ore.

text: In electroplating a key with nickel, the key is made the:
explanation: The object to be plated is always the cathode (metal deposits here). The anode is the plating metal (nickel). [Board 2019] Anode dissolves; either electrode is wrong; electrolyte is the solution.

text: A gas produced when dilute HCl reacts with Na₂S that turns lead acetate paper black:
explanation: Na₂S + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H₂S↑. H₂S turns Pb(CH₃COO)₂ paper black (PbS). [Board 2019] HCl turns moist blue litmus red; SO₂ turns acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ green; SO₃ reacts violently with water.

text: Which of the following is an example of an acid salt?
explanation: NaHSO₄ (sodium bisulphate) is an acid salt — partially neutralised acid still has replaceable H⁺. [Board 2019] Na₂SO₄ is a normal salt; NaCl is a normal salt; NaOH is a base not a salt.

text: In the reaction N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃, 28 g N₂ reacts with hydrogen to produce:
explanation: 28 g N₂ = 1 mol. Produces 2 mol NH₃ = 2×17 = 34 g. [Board 2020] 17 g = 1 mol NH₃; 51 g = 3 mol; 68 g = 4 mol.

text: Homologous series of compounds with general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH is:
explanation: CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH = alkanols (alcohols). n=1: CH₃OH; n=2: C₂H₅OH etc. [Board 2020] Alkanes = CₙH₂ₙ₊₂; Alkenes = CₙH₂ₙ; Acids = CₙH₂ₙO₂.

text: The number of lone pairs of electrons on the nitrogen atom in NH₃:
explanation: N has 5 valence electrons. 3 are shared in N-H bonds. 2 remaining form 1 lone pair. [Board 2020] 0 lone pairs = BH₃; 2 lone pairs = O in H₂O; 3 lone pairs = Cl in HCl.

text: The quantity of electricity needed to deposit 1 mol of a divalent metal (n=2) using Faraday's laws is:
explanation: Charge = n × F = 2 × 96500 = 2 Faradays. For monovalent metal = 1F; divalent = 2F; trivalent = 3F. [Board 2020]

text: Chlorine gas is produced in the laboratory by reacting:
explanation: MnO₂ + 4HCl(conc.) → MnCl₂ + Cl₂ + 2H₂O. [Board 2020] NaCl+dilute H₂SO₄ gives HCl gas; NaCl+water gives NaCl solution; dilute HCl doesn't oxidise to Cl₂.

text: The pH of a solution is 3. The solution is:
explanation: pH < 7 means acidic. pH = 3 is strongly acidic. [Board 2020] Basic = pH>7; Neutral = pH=7; weakly basic = pH 7.1 to 10.

text: Stainless steel is an alloy of iron containing:
explanation: Stainless steel = Fe + Cr (12-18%) + Ni (8%). Cr prevents rusting; Ni adds hardness. [Board 2020] Carbon added gives high-carbon steel not stainless; Zn+Cu = brass; Sn+Pb = solder.

text: The element with electronic configuration 2,8,7 belongs to:
explanation: Valence electrons = 7 → Group 17. Shells = 3 → Period 3. [Board 2020] Group 7 is transition metals; Period 17 doesn't exist; Period 2 has only 8 electrons maximum.

text: A white precipitate forms when NaOH is added to a salt solution and dissolves in excess NaOH. The metal ion is:
explanation: Zn(OH)₂ is white, amphoteric — dissolves in excess NaOH to form [Zn(OH)₄]²⁻. [Board 2020] Fe(OH)₃ is reddish-brown; Cu(OH)₂ is blue; Ca(OH)₂ is sparingly soluble and doesn't dissolve.

text: Number of molecules in 4.4 g of CO₂ (M=44):
Sodium carbonate reacts with excess HCl to give:
explanation: Na₂CO₃ + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H₂O + CO₂↑ (excess HCl drives complete reaction). [Board 2023] NaHCO₃ forms with limited HCl; Na₂CO₃ doesn't remain; Na₂O is the anhydrous base.

text: Fermentation of glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆) by yeast produces:
explanation: C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂ (zymase enzyme from yeast). [Board 2023] CH₄ is anaerobic digestion; ethanol + water is not balanced; acetic acid is from vinegar bacteria.

text: Which of the following molecules contains a double bond?
explanation: CO₂ = O=C=O has two double bonds. [Board 2023] H₂O has single bonds; NH₃ has single bonds; HCl has single bond.

text: The empirical formula of a compound with 40% C, 6.67% H, 53.33% O (by mass) is:
explanation: Ratio: C=40/12=3.33, H=6.67/1=6.67, O=53.33/16=3.33. Simplify: C:H:O = 1:2:1 = CH₂O. [Board 2023] C₂H₄O₂ = molecular formula (×2); CHO gives wrong H ratio; C₃H₆O₃ = molecular formula (×3).

text: Carbon dioxide turns lime water milky because:
explanation: CO₂ + Ca(OH)₂ → CaCO₃↓ + H₂O. CaCO₃ is insoluble white precipitate (milky). [Board 2023] Ca(OH)₂ is slightly soluble and doesn't dissolve more; CO₂ acidity is the cause but precipitate is CaCO₃; Ca is a metal.

text: The cathode in electrolysis of CuSO₄ using copper electrodes is made of:
explanation: In electroplating with copper, cathode is the object to be plated (can be copper) and anode is pure copper. [Board 2023] Carbon is used for inert electrode; platinum for acidic solutions; iron would also plate but it's not standard.

text: Across a period, which property increases steadily?
explanation: Electronegativity increases across a period (left to right) due to increasing nuclear charge. [Board 2023] Atomic radius decreases; metallic character decreases; reactivity pattern varies across metals and non-metals.

text: Which property of iron makes it useful for making nails and tools?
explanation: Iron is hard and has high tensile strength, suitable for nails, tools and structural work. [Board 2023] Iron has a high melting point (1538°C); copper has higher conductivity; aluminium is lighter.

text: A blue precipitate formed with NaOH identifies which cation?
explanation: Cu²⁺ + 2NaOH → Cu(OH)₂ (blue precipitate). [Board 2023] Fe²⁺ gives dirty green; Fe³⁺ gives reddish-brown; Zn²⁺ gives white precipitate.

text: The indicator that changes colour in the range pH 8.2 to 10 is:
explanation: Phenolphthalein is colourless below pH 8.2 and pink/red above 10. [Board 2023] Litmus changes at pH 7; methyl orange changes at pH 3.1–4.4; universal indicator shows a range of colours.

text: Unsaturated hydrocarbons undergo:
explanation: Unsaturated hydrocarbons (alkenes, alkynes) have double/triple bonds that readily undergo addition reactions (e.g., halogenation, hydrogenation). Substitution is for saturated (alkanes); oxidation and redox are not the primary reaction type.

text: In the 2nd period, Neon has maximum Ionization Potential because:
options: The outermost shell is completely filled
explanation: Neon has a completely filled outermost shell (2,8), giving it a very stable noble gas configuration. This makes it hardest to remove an electron. Noble gases neither accept nor lose electrons easily.

text: Copper, Zinc and Tin are the metals alloyed to form:
explanation: Bronze is an alloy of Copper and Tin (sometimes with Zinc). Brass is Cu+Zn only; Duralumin is Al+Cu+Mn+Mg; Solder is Pb+Sn. The presence of Copper, Zinc AND Tin together points to Bronze (gun metal variant).

text: The metal hydroxide which reacts with both acids and alkalis to form salt and water is:
explanation: Aluminium hydroxide Al(OH)₃ is amphoteric — it reacts with both acids (forms AlCl₃) and strong bases (forms aluminate). Ca(OH)₂ and Mg(OH)₂ are basic only; Fe(OH)₃ is a basic hydroxide.

text: Reaction of an alcohol with a carboxylic acid in presence of concentrated H₂SO₄ is termed:
explanation: Esterification: alcohol + carboxylic acid → ester + water (H₂SO₄ is catalyst). Halogenation adds halogens; hydrogenation adds hydrogen; dehydrohalogenation removes HX from haloalkanes.

text: Conversion of Ethanol to Ethene by action of concentrated sulphuric acid involves:
explanation: Dehydration removes water (H₂O) from ethanol (C₂H₅OH) using hot conc. H₂SO₄ to form ethene (C₂H₄). Dehydrogenation removes H₂; dehydrohalogenation removes HX; hydrolysis adds water.

text: The oxidizing agent in S + 2H₂SO₄ → 3SO₂ + 2H₂O is:
explanation: H₂SO₄ gets reduced to SO₂ (S goes from +6 to +4), so it is the oxidizing agent. Sulphur gets oxidized (0 to +4) — it's the reducing agent. SO₂ and H₂O are products, not reactants in the oxidation sense.

text: Electron Affinity is maximum in:
explanation: Electron affinity is highest for halogens (Group 17). Bromine (Br) has high electron affinity as it gains an electron to complete its octet. Mg and Li are metals (low EA); Ar is a noble gas (essentially zero EA).

text: The compound NOT a constituent of the electrolytic mixture used in Hall-Heroult's process is:
explanation: Hall-Heroult process uses Al₂O₃ (alumina) dissolved in Na₃AlF₆ (cryolite) with CaF₂ to lower melting point. NaAlO₂ (sodium aluminate) is NOT part of this electrolytic mixture.

text: Passing ammonia gas over heated copper oxide leaves a reddish-brown residue. This demonstrates ammonia's property as:
explanation: Ammonia reduces CuO to Cu (reddish-brown) while NH₃ is oxidized to N₂. This demonstrates the reducing property of NH₃. CuO is reduced, so NH₃ is the reducer, not oxidizer or base.

text: Rotten egg smell is due to liberation of:
explanation: H₂S (hydrogen sulphide) has the characteristic rotten egg smell. HCl is pungent/acidic smell; Cl₂ has bleaching/irritating smell; SO₂ has a sharp, choking smell.

text: Ammonia gas is collected by downward displacement of air since ammonia is:
explanation: Ammonia (molecular weight 17) is lighter than air (average MW ~29), so it rises and displaces air downward. It is also highly soluble in water (so cannot collect over water). It's collected by downward displacement of air.

text: Which would occupy 22.4 litres at STP? 1. 32g of oxygen 2. 2 moles of hydrogen 3. 6.022×10²³ molecules of ammonia
explanation: 1 mole of any gas = 22.4L at STP. 1: 32g O₂ = 1 mole = 22.4L ✓. 2: 2 moles H₂ = 44.8L ✗. 3: 6.022×10²³ molecules = 1 mole NH₃ = 22.4L ✓. So 1 & 3 (option B). Wait: option C says 2 & 3. Option B (1 & 3) is correct.

text: In a water molecule, the oxygen atom has:
explanation: Oxygen in H₂O has 2 shared pairs (O–H bonds) and 2 lone pairs. Total 4 electron pairs. 'One shared pair' is wrong (there are 2); 'three shared' is wrong; 'one lone pair' is wrong (two lone pairs).

text: Which gas is evolved at the anode during electrolysis of dilute sulphuric acid?
explanation: At anode (positive electrode), oxidation occurs: 2H₂O → O₂ + 4H⁺ + 4e⁻. Oxygen is evolved. Hydrogen is at cathode; SO₂ and Cl₂ are not produced from H₂SO₄ solution electrolysis.

text: Which gas decolourises potassium permanganate (KMnO₄) solution?
explanation: SO₂ is a reducing agent that decolourises acidified KMnO₄ (purple to colourless) by reducing Mn⁷⁺ to Mn²⁺. NH₃, HCl, and CO₂ don't decolourise KMnO₄.

text: Which formula represents a saturated hydrocarbon?
explanation: Saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes) follow CₙH₂ₙ₊₂. C₅H₁₂: 2(5)+2=12 ✓. C₄H₈ = CₙH₂ₙ (alkene); C₄H₆ = CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ (alkyne); C₅H₁₀ = CₙH₂ₙ (alkene/cycloalkane).

text: The metal whose oxide can be reduced by common reducing agents:
explanation: Copper is a less reactive metal (low in activity series). CuO can be easily reduced by C, CO, H₂, etc. Sodium, Potassium, and Aluminium are too reactive — their oxides cannot be reduced by common reducing agents.

text: An organic compound has vapour density of 22. The molecular formula is: [C=12, H=1]
explanation: Molecular mass = 2 × vapour density = 2×22 = 44. C₂H₆: 24+6=30 (no). C₃H₈: 36+8=44 ✓. Actually C₃H₈ = 44. So answer should be (d). Let me check: CH₄=16, C₂H₄=28, C₂H₆=30, C₃H₈=44. Answer is C₃H₈ (option d).

text: In the reaction S + 2H₂SO₄ → 3SO₂ + 2H₂O, sulphuric acid acts as:
explanation: H₂SO₄ gets reduced (S: +6→+4 in SO₂), so it is the oxidising agent. Sulphur gets oxidised (0→+4). While H₂SO₄ is non-volatile and dibasic, these are not the property demonstrated in this specific reaction.

text: Assertion: Tendency of losing electrons increases down Group 1. Reason: The most reactive metal is placed at the top of Group 1. Which is correct?
options: Both A and R true, R is correct explanation
Both A and R true, R is not correct explanation
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: A is true: metallic character increases down a group (easier to lose electrons). R is false: the MOST reactive metal in Group 1 is at the BOTTOM (Caesium), not the top (Lithium is least reactive). So A is true, R is false.

text: The ore that can be concentrated by magnetic separation:
explanation: Haematite (Fe₂O₃) is magnetic and can be separated from gangue using magnetic separators. Corundum (Al₂O₃), Calamine (ZnCO₃), and Bauxite (Al₂O₃.2H₂O) are non-magnetic.

text: Which option has all compounds from the same homologous series?
explanation: Alkane series (CₙH₂ₙ₊₂): CH₄, C₂H₆, C₃H₈ differ by CH₂ each — same homologous series. Option B mixes alkane and alkene; Option C has same carbon, different unsaturation; Option D mixes alkene and alkane.

text: In Contact Process, SO₃ is not dissolved directly in water because:
options: Both A and R true, R is correct explanation
Both A and R true, R is not correct explanation
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: A is true: SO₃ is absorbed in conc. H₂SO₄, not water directly. R is true: direct dissolution forms dense acid mist/fog that is hard to condense. R correctly explains why water is not used — so both true and R is correct explanation.

text: Given ions Cl⁻, Li⁺, Al³⁺, K⁺. Which pair has the same electronic configuration? [Cl=17, Li=3, Al=13, K=19]
explanation: Cl⁻ (17+1=18e⁻): 2,8,8. K⁺ (19–1=18e⁻): 2,8,8. Both have 18 electrons (argon configuration). Li⁺ has 2e⁻; Al³⁺ has 10e⁻ (neon config). Cl⁻ and K⁺ match.

text: Which pair of reactants can best be used to produce lead(II) sulphate?
explanation: Lead sulphate (PbSO₄) is insoluble. Na₂SO₄ + Pb(NO₃)₂ → PbSO₄↓ + 2NaNO₃ (double displacement, precipitation). Lead reacts slowly with H₂SO₄; Pb(OH)₂ + H₂SO₄ gives soluble product issues; K₂SO₄ + PbO also works but is less common in practice.

text: Aqueous copper sulphate is electrolysed using inert electrodes. What is deposited at the cathode?
explanation: At cathode (reduction): Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu. Copper metal is deposited. At anode: 2H₂O → O₂ + 4H⁺ + 4e⁻. Oxygen is released at anode, not cathode. Hydrogen is released when H₂SO₄ is very dilute.

text: The element with electronic configuration 2,8,7 belongs to:
explanation: Outermost shell has 7 electrons → Group 17 (halogens). Three shells (2,8,7) → Period 3. The element is Chlorine (Cl, atomic number 17).

text: Which salt solution turns moist blue litmus red and also gives a white precipitate with AgNO₃ solution?
explanation: NH₄Cl: acidic solution (NH₄⁺ hydrolyzes) turns blue litmus red, AND Cl⁻ + Ag⁺ → AgCl↓ (white precipitate). Sulphate gives white ppt with BaCl₂; carbonate is alkaline; nitrate gives no precipitate with AgNO₃.

text: The type of bond present in ammonium chloride (NH₄Cl) includes:
explanation: NH₄Cl has: ionic bond (NH₄⁺ and Cl⁻), covalent bonds (N–H bonds in NH₄⁺), and one coordinate bond (N donates lone pair to H⁺ to form NH₄⁺). All three types are present.

text: A non-metal which reacts with concentrated sulphuric acid to form two gases which turn lime water milky is:
explanation: Carbon + 2H₂SO₄(conc.) → CO₂↑ + 2SO₂↑ + 2H₂O. Both CO₂ and SO₂ turn lime water milky. Sulphur gives SO₂ only; Oxygen doesn't react this way; Nitrogen is unreactive with H₂SO₄.

text: Which pair of elements will form an ionic bond? P: Group1&2; Q: Group14&16; R: Group2&17; S: Group15&18
explanation: Ionic bonds form between metals (Groups 1,2) and non-metals (Group 17). Group 2 + Group 17 (e.g., MgCl₂) readily forms ionic bonds. Group 14+16 form covalent bonds; Group 1+2 form metallic bonds; Group 18 doesn't bond.

text: Electronic configuration of element is 2,8,2. The hydroxide of this element can produce ___ hydroxyl ions per molecule.
explanation: 2,8,2 is Magnesium (Mg, Group 2). Mg(OH)₂ has 2 hydroxyl ions. Group 2 metals form M(OH)₂. 3 hydroxyl ions would be Group 3 (Al(OH)₃); 1 would be Group 1 (NaOH); 0 would be a non-metal oxide.

text: Electrolysis of copper sulphate solution using copper electrodes — which statement is correct?
options: Copper is deposited at negative electrode
Oxygen gas is produced at positive electrode
The positive electrode increases in mass
The negative electrode decreases in mass
explanation: At cathode (negative): Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu (copper deposited). At anode (copper electrode): Cu → Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ (anode dissolves, DECREASES in mass). Options B, C, D are incorrect.

text: Identify the equation showing reaction of ethane with chlorine in UV light:
explanation: Alkanes undergo substitution with halogens in UV light: C₂H₆ + Cl₂ → C₂H₅Cl + HCl (one H replaced by Cl). Option A would be addition (alkane can't do addition); B removes H₂ (wrong); D breaks carbon-carbon bond (wrong).

text: Rita added dilute HCl to four metals. Which observation(s) are correct? 1-copper(gas given off), 2-iron(gas given off), 3-magnesium(no gas), 4-zinc(gas given off)
explanation: Iron and Zinc react with dilute HCl to give H₂ gas. Copper does NOT react with dilute HCl (too low in activity series). Magnesium DOES react vigorously with HCl. So: 1 is wrong (Cu doesn't react), 3 is wrong (Mg does react), 2 and 4 are correct.

text: An atom X forms ion X²⁺. The atomic number of X is:
explanation: X²⁺ means X loses 2 electrons. Mg (atomic number 12) forms Mg²⁺. Configuration: 2,8,2 → loses 2 → 2,8 (stable). S(16) forms S²⁻; Ne(10) is noble gas; Si(14) rarely forms +2 ion.

text: Dilute acid on bases, carbonates, metals, sulphites can make salts. Which method CANNOT be used for copper salts?
explanation: Copper is below hydrogen in reactivity series — it does NOT react with dilute acids to give H₂ or copper salt. All other methods (reacting CuO, Cu(OH)₂, CuCO₃, CuSO₃ with dilute acid) work to make copper salts.

text: The compound with the highest melting point amongst the following is:
explanation: NaCl (ionic compound) has very high melting point (~801°C) due to strong ionic lattice. Methane (–182°C), Ammonia (–78°C), Ethanol (–114°C) are molecular compounds with much lower melting points.

text: Assertion: Dilute H₂SO₄ is a stronger electrolyte than concentrated H₂SO₄. Reason: Dilute H₂SO₄ has higher concentration of mobile ions. Which is correct?
options: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R true, R is correct explanation
Both A and R true, R is not correct explanation
explanation: Both are true: Dilute H₂SO₄ is more ionized (more mobile H⁺ and SO₄²⁻ ions) than concentrated H₂SO₄ (which is less ionized). R correctly explains A — more dissociation in dilute solution → stronger electrolyte.
